reader: Claude Fable 5.2, research reader with the source at hand
reason: The first reading was made without a source; comparison with the 1501 print of the Sermones Amici settled abbreviated and damaged words in all eight columns.
sources: Sermones Amici ex corrupto reintegrati ([Basel: Nikolaus Kesler] 1501, VD16 S 6046), Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, 4 P.lat. 1540, bsb10990936, scans 9, 10, 16 and 17 (fols. III recto to VII recto), page images
S. Bonaventurae Opera omnia, ed. A. C. Peltier, vol. 13 (Paris 1868), pp. 142-143, machine-read text at archive.org (operaomniasixtiv13bonauoft)
text:
Source-assisted reading of F-da74 (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 45). All eight column tops (four lines each) were reread on the native images and then compared with Sermones Amici ex corrupto reintegrati ([Basel: Kesler] 1501), BSB bsb10990936, scans 9, 10, 16 and 17. Round brackets = abbreviations expanded; square brackets = lost or cut, supplied from the print; ? = uncertain. Columns are given in the order of the text.

LEAF 1 RECTO = face labelled 45v, right half (canvas 1, Stams_STA_Frg_045_01v)

col. a, native box 3900,2650-4900,3080  [Amicus, distinction II]
1  q(ui)dem p(ro)mpt(us) est caro au(tem) inf(ir)-
2  ma. Un(de) (con)formans se d(iv)i(n)e? [vo]-
3  lu(n)tati sa(n)g(ui)ne(m)? sudar(e) cepit et
4  hoc totu(m) ad salute(m) mea(m). Un(de)
5  T[u]llius [...]   (cut through)

col. b, native box 4850,2650-5850,3080
1  a flagellis et(er)ne? ire? te erip(er)et? [pro]   (line damaged by holes; words after "flagellis" guided by the print)
2  te coronat(us) est spinis ut te co-
3  ronet in celis. P(ro) te vuln(er)at(us)?   (uncertain; an earlier reading had humiliatus)
4  est medic(us) ut tu salv(er)is? inf(ir)m(us)   (tall l after "sa"; the print has sanareris)

LEAF 1 VERSO = face labelled 45r, left half (canvas 0, Stams_STA_Frg_045_01r)

col. a, native box 1650,2780-2800,3160  [end of Amicus II]
1  [paupere]m? (Christu)m natu(m) sine hospitio
2  int(er) bove(m) (et) asinu(m) iacente(m) i(n) p(re)-
3  sepio fugiente(m) in egyptu(m) sedente(m)
4  in asina nudu(m) pendentem i(n) patib(u)lo

col. b, native box 2700,2780-3900,3160  [Ascendere, distinction I]
1  custodiret immune(m). 2m fuit ex-
2  cellens ip(s)ius humilitas. Un(de)
3  Luc. i? [red paraph] Ecce ancilla d(omi)ni fiat   (underlined in red)
4  m(ihi) s(ecundu)m v(er)bu(m) tuu(m). Ancilla p(er)fecte?

LEAF 2 RECTO = face labelled 45r, right half (canvas 0)

col. a, native box 4400,2780-5350,3160  [Converti]
1  nos inseq(ue)ris tenes (et) abii-
2  c(er)is dorsu(m) av(er)tim(us) i(n) facie(m)
3  occ(ur)ris (et) supplicas (et) d(e)spi-
4  c(er)is s(ed) nulla te despectio?

col. b, native box 5400,2780-6250,3160
1  mea(m)(?) sic(ut) torrens [in] aus[tro flante]   (right end lost)
2  eni(m) aust(r)o calido i(d est) sp[iritu sancto]
3  solvit(ur) glacies p(e)cc(a)to(rum) [currunt]
4  torrentes lac(ri)ma(rum). [red paraph] Un[de]

LEAF 2 VERSO = face labelled 45v, left half (canvas 1)

col. a, native box 1500,2650-2400,3080
1  [p]otentia(m) tua(m) et veni et? sal[vos]
2  [f]acias nos. [red stroke] Ecce D(avi)d d[ei potenti]-
3  [a](m) invocat ut nos salvos [faciat]
4  et (con)v(er)tat. Infi(ni)ta(m) eni(m)

col. b, native box 2400,2650-3500,3080
1  peccavi no(n) desp(er)o q(uia) sup(ra)
2  modu(m) doluit in q(u)o respi(r)o
3  exac(er)babit(ur) p(ate)r i(m)manitate
4  sceleris mei mitigabit(ur) in

Not read: the large mirror-image letters in the upper margin of 45v (offset from another leaf).
